title: A Multi-Layered AI-IoT Framework for Adaptive Financial Services
authors: Garg, A.; Pandey, M.; Pathak, A. R.
venue: International Journal of Emerging Trends in Computer Science and Information Technology
tldr: A three-layer AI-IoT framework integrating edge computing, federated learning, and zero-trust security achieves 89% fraud detection accuracy, 19.4% customer satisfaction improvement, and 65.2% latency reduction in simulated banking deployment.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional banking systems rely on static, rules-based fraud detection and manual personalization, resulting in 39% false positive rates and 2.3-second response latencies. The convergence of IoT sensor data and AI analytics remains fragmented, with no unified architecture for real-time adaptive financial services. Banks need scalable frameworks that balance hyper-personalization with data privacy and security compliance.
approach: Proposed a three-layer conceptual framework consisting of Input Layer (IoT endpoints), Intelligence Layer (AI analytics), and Experience Layer (user interfaces).
Integrated edge computing to reduce latency by processing data at smart ATMs and wearable devices rather than centralized servers.
Applied federated learning to train AI models across edge devices without uploading raw sensitive data to central repositories.
Implemented zero-trust architecture with continuous verification at every layer to prevent spoofing, injection, and data exfiltration.
Designed modular architecture adaptable to multinational banking ecosystems or smaller fintech environments.
Evaluated the framework through simulation of a mid-sized digital banking entity across urban centers in Africa and Asia over 12 months.
Benchmarked against traditional banking systems on fraud detection rate, customer satisfaction index, response latency, and false positive rate.
findings: num: Fraud detection accuracy improved from 60% to 89%, a +48.3% increase after AI-IoT deployment.
num: False positive rate decreased from 39% to 11%, a -71.8% reduction in erroneous fraud flags.
num: Customer Satisfaction Index rose from 72/100 to 86/100, a +19.4% improvement.
num: Average response latency dropped from 2.3 seconds to 0.8 seconds, a -65.2% reduction.
num: Edge computing reduces latency by eliminating uplink, cloud processing, and downlink transmission steps.
num: Initial infrastructure investment recovered within 8 months through operational cost savings.
num: Customer churn rate decreased by 14% following AI-IoT deployment.
Federated AI for biometric KYC accelerated onboarding by 50% while mitigating data breach risk.

definitions.definition: Internet of Things - network of interconnected devices collecting and exchanging data in real time.
Artificial Intelligence - computational systems capable of learning, reasoning, and making decisions from data.

Near Field Communication - short-range wireless technology enabling contactless transactions.
Know Your Customer - identity verification process for financial institutions.
Explainable Artificial Intelligence - AI systems designed to provide transparent, interpretable decision rationales.
Customer Satisfaction Index - metric measuring post-interaction satisfaction levels.
Net Promoter Score - customer loyalty metric based on likelihood to recommend.
Banking as a Service - platform model enabling non-bank entities to offer financial services.
General Data Protection Regulation - EU regulation governing data privacy and protection.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a unified three-layer conceptual framework for integrating IoT and AI in banking services, addressing the gap between fragmented technology implementations and holistic intelligent banking architectures. It provides a systematic evaluation of edge computing, federated learning, and zero-trust security as enabling technologies for real-time financial services. The study establishes quantitative benchmarks for fraud detection, customer satisfaction, and latency reduction in AI-IoT banking deployments. It also addresses critical security and privacy challenges specific to interconnected financial systems, proposing mitigations including federated learning and micro-segmentation.
directly_justifies: AI-IoT framework achieves 89% fraud detection accuracy compared to 60% in traditional systems.
Edge computing reduces average decision latency from 2.3 seconds to 0.8 seconds.
Federated learning enables model training without sharing raw sensitive data across banking devices.
Zero-trust architecture with continuous verification prevents lateral movement attacks in IoT banking networks.
limits: Framework evaluation relies on simulated deployment rather than production-scale empirical testing.
The study does not provide open-source implementation or reproducible benchmarks for validation.
Security analysis focuses on known attack vectors without adversarial robustness testing.
Scalability claims are not validated against actual multi-region banking traffic patterns.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) was flagged as high relevance for its comprehensive comparison of traditional vs. AI-IoT banking. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was assigned high relevance for credit scoring and transaction forecasting models. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) was flagged as high for real-time fraud detection using anomaly scores. Domains 9 (Mobile-First Design) were assigned medium relevance for mobile and wearable banking interfaces. Domain 10 (Data Privacy and Security) received high relevance for federated learning and zero-trust architecture contributions. Domain 11 (Engagement) was assigned medium relevance for emotion-aware interfaces reducing churn. Domain 14 (ML Deployment) received high relevance for edge computing and on-device inference architecture. Borderline cases included Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles), considered but rejected as the paper does not focus on profile classification. Domain 7 (Budgeting) was rejected as budget recommendation is not addressed. The paper's coverage spans infrastructure, security, and application layers of AI-driven financial services.

limitations: Simulation-based evaluation lacks validation against real production banking environments with adversarial conditions.
The conceptual framework has not been implemented as open-source software for community validation.
Security analysis does not include adversarial robustness testing against sophisticated attack scenarios.
Scalability claims are not empirically tested across actual multi-region banking traffic volumes.
The paper does not address regulatory compliance beyond GDPR, limiting applicability to diverse jurisdictions.
